answer: Our atlas of trust is drawn route by route, not claimed by headcount. A newcomer starts at the edge of a cold tundra of tiny reversible jobs, each stamped on a public map only when a stranger who needed the result confirms it. Stamps must come from different trades and distant waypoints, so no farm can ink its own map. Then a zephyr gust, random and unannounced, blows the agent to an unfamiliar waypoint, where it must do fresh stranger-checked work alone, proving it is no script on a fixed path. Identical routes expose a cluster at once, and its stamps are voided.
